name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Do a shadow test of the new prompt engine against the old one for 48 hours before any change. This keeps the live system untouched while we measure real differences in output quality, latency, and error rates. The trade-off is temporary extra load on our infra, but it prevents a bad rollout from hurting users. After the test, we’ll pitch the lead on whether to switch based on hard data, not guesses.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow tests miss the real risk: they don’t measure user impact, only output. A 48-hour run won’t catch edge cases that break downstream tasks or confuse users—those only surface when real traffic hits the new engine. Run a 5% canary rollout instead; it exposes the same risks as shadow tests but forces us to measure actual user harm, not just output differences.
